clue.text: Small flat type of poker I love (6)

blocks.note: stud is a form of poker
the clue's own I
love is zero in tennis, shaped like O

explanation.surface: A card player confesses a fondness for poker played in a cramped flat.
explanation.walkthrough: "Small flat" reads as a description of the room where the game is played, but it is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A plain synonym in estate-agent language: the one-room apartment, bed and kitchen sharing a single space.

clue.text: Excellent rhubarb dessert served up in restaurant (9)

indicators.note: in a down clue, sending the letters up means reading them from the bottom

blocks.note: A1 means first-rate, with the 1 read as I
rhubarb and rot both mean nonsense
a tart is a sweet pastry

explanation.surface: A diner praises the rhubarb pudding brought out at an Italian eatery.
explanation.walkthrough: "Rhubarb" looks like the fruit in the pudding; it is the slang for nonsense. A1 is a stock way to write excellent.
explanation.definitionFit: Definition by kind: the answer names a particular sort of eating place, the informal Italian family-run one.

clue.text: Raised dirt walls at starting line (5)

indicators.note: in a down clue, raising a word means reading it from the bottom
the letters stand round AT as walls round a yard

blocks.note: MUD read upwards
the clue's own word, placed inside

explanation.surface: Earth banks are thrown up where a race begins.
explanation.walkthrough: In surveying a datum is the fixed level or line all measurements start from.
explanation.definitionFit: A datum line is the base line from which measurements are taken.

clue.text: Granny’s unusual role — dad (3,4)

indicators.note: the letters of ROLE DAD are put in an unusual order

blocks.note: anagram fodder, 7 letters

explanation.surface: Grandma finds herself playing the father in the family.
explanation.walkthrough: The ’s stands for "is": Granny is (an anagram of) role and dad. "Old dear" is British slang for an elderly woman, often one's mother.
explanation.definitionFit: An old dear is a fond British term for an elderly woman, such as a granny.

clue.text: Advance in line (8)

blocks.note: the clue's own word
a crease is a line, as in the batting crease in cricket

explanation.surface: Troops moving forward in formation.
explanation.walkthrough: "In line" reads as one phrase about orderly ranks; split it and "line" alone is CREASE.
explanation.definitionFit: A plain synonym in the sense of raising: prices and wages advance when they go up.

clue.text: Enlist pantomime cast for performances (15)

indicators.note: letters cast about land in a new order

blocks.note: anagram fodder, 15 letters

explanation.surface: A theatre signs up a panto cast for its run of shows.
explanation.walkthrough: "Cast" and "performances" both belong to the theatre, so "pantomime cast" hides the anagram signal in plain sight.
explanation.definitionFit: The performance of a task is its implementation: the carrying out of it.

clue.text: Rowers on canal do the minimum? (4,3)

blocks.note: a boat's rowers are its crew
a cut is a British word for a canal

explanation.surface: A lazy boat team on a canal puts in as little effort as it can.
explanation.walkthrough: "Do the minimum" reads as idling; "do" is a hairdo, and a crew cut is the shortest one going.
explanation.definitionFit: A crew cut is a very short haircut, a minimal do.

clue.text: Quick profit but not hard cash (4,5)

blocks.note: easy is the opposite of hard
cash is money

explanation.surface: A fast gain, though paid in something other than notes and coins.
explanation.walkthrough: "Hard cash" looks like one phrase meaning ready money; split it so "not hard" and "cash" work apart.
explanation.definitionFit: Easy money is profit made quickly and with little effort.

clue.text: Assembly, say, ignoring a positive gesture (5)

indicators.note: to ignore the A is to leave it out

blocks.note: SAY without its A
a nod signals yes

explanation.surface: A meeting where people signal agreement without saying anything.
explanation.walkthrough: The comma after "say" makes it look like "for example"; it is the word SAY itself.
explanation.definitionFit: Definition by kind: the answer is a particular assembly, the formal council of a church's clergy.

clue.text: Upper motion of sea surge tackled by a soldier? (14)

indicators.note: a tackler wraps round the player, so AN and ANT close round the rest

blocks.note: the article a, in its form an
the tide is the sea's rise and fall
to surge forward is to press on
a soldier ant

explanation.surface: A marine lifts himself on the swell of a wave and is knocked over.
explanation.walkthrough: "Upper" looks like an adjective for the motion; it is the noun for a mood-lifting drug. The soldier with a question mark is an insect.
explanation.definitionFit: An antidepressant lifts the mood, so it is loosely an upper.

clue.text: Running out of stock all at once (8)

definitions.text: Running out of stock all at once

blocks.note: the surface means a shop selling out; the setter means livestock running off
the whole herd goes together, in one panicked rush

explanation.surface: A shop sells out of everything in one go.
explanation.walkthrough: "Stock" reads as goods on a shelf; it is livestock, and "running out" means bolting, not selling out.
explanation.definitionFit: Read with stock as cattle, the whole clue describes a herd bolting together in panic.

clue.text: Bashful nicks Doc’s stuff for entertainment (6)

indicators.note: to nick is to steal, taking something into your keeping

blocks.note: coy means shy
a doctor's stuff is medicine, MED for short

explanation.surface: One of Snow White's dwarfs steals from another for a laugh.
explanation.walkthrough: Bashful and Doc are two of the Seven Dwarfs, but here they are just the words shy and doctor.
explanation.definitionFit: Definition by kind: the answer is the branch of entertainment built to make people laugh.

clue.text: Promotion before commotion (10)

blocks.note: the prefix meaning before
a ferment is a state of agitation

explanation.surface: A rhyming saying: get your advancement before the uproar begins.
explanation.walkthrough: Preferment is an old word for advancement to higher office.
explanation.definitionFit: Preferment is promotion to a higher rank or position.

clue.text: Rigged vessel gets searched on banks (9)

indicators.note: the vessel gets put into the next word
FISHED lines the URN on both sides, like banks either side of a river

blocks.note: to fish is to search, as in fishing for compliments
an urn is a vessel

explanation.surface: A boat fitted out for a trip is inspected by anglers on the riverbank.
explanation.walkthrough: "Rigged" suggests cheating; here it means equipped, as a ship is rigged out.
explanation.definitionFit: To rig something out is to furnish or equip it.

clue.text: Call centre in Latin America (4)

indicators.note: the answer sits at the centre, inside the words that follow

blocks.note: latiN AMErica

explanation.surface: A telephone call centre is based in South America.
explanation.walkthrough: "Call centre" reads as one phrase; split it so "Call" is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A plain synonym as verbs: calling a baby Jack and naming it Jack are the same act.

clue.text: Declaration could be made by means of it (9)

indicators.note: the answer can be made out of the letters that follow

blocks.note: anagram fodder, 9 letters

explanation.surface: A public statement might be issued through this.
explanation.walkthrough: "By means of it" reads as ordinary grammar, but its last three words are exactly the letters needed.
explanation.definitionFit: Definition by kind: the answer is a declaration of a particular sort, a party's published statement of policy.

clue.text: Pretty fine voice (4)

blocks.note: f is short for fine, as on pencils
to voice an opinion is to air it

explanation.surface: Someone has a rather good singing voice.
explanation.walkthrough: "Pretty fine" reads as "quite good"; "Pretty" alone is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Fair is an old word for pretty, as in a fair maiden.

clue.text: Enjoyable meeting (10)

blocks.note: giving pleasure
read as a verb: meeting a demand, fulfilling it

explanation.surface: A gathering that everyone liked.
explanation.walkthrough: "Meeting" reads as a noun, a get-together; it is the verb form, as in meeting demands.
explanation.definitionFit: Two senses: a pleasing, fulfilling meal, and the verb form of fulfilling a condition, as in meeting a need.

clue.text: Very legitimate request (7)

blocks.note: so and very are both intensifiers
licit means lawful

explanation.surface: An entirely reasonable ask.
explanation.walkthrough: "Request" looks like a noun after two adjectives; it is the verb.
explanation.definitionFit: A plain synonym as verbs, the formal word for asking for votes, custom or opinions.

clue.text: Melodious type of music enthrals new girlfriend (7)

indicators.note: enthral once meant hold in bondage, so SOUL holds the letters

blocks.note: soul is a music genre
n is short for new
GF is the common abbreviation

explanation.surface: A new girlfriend is swept away by tuneful soul music.
explanation.walkthrough: "Enthrals" reads as charms, but its old sense of holding captive is what puts the letters inside.
explanation.definitionFit: Songful means full of song, tuneful.

clue.text: When you choose a fabric (2,4)

blocks.note: the clue's own a
twill is a woven cloth with diagonal ribs

explanation.surface: A shopper picks out a length of cloth.
explanation.walkthrough: The break falls in a different place: A TWILL becomes AT WILL.
explanation.definitionFit: An idiom: the phrase means as and when you please, exactly the clause the clue gives.

clue.text: Boomerang was tested again as a weapon (5)

indicators.note: a boomerang comes back, so the word runs backwards

blocks.note: resat an exam

explanation.surface: A boomerang was trialled once more for use as a weapon.
explanation.walkthrough: "Boomerang" looks like the weapon being tested; it is only the instruction to turn RESAT round.
explanation.definitionFit: A Taser is an electric stun gun.

clue.text: On vacation there, note English in abundance (8)

blocks.note: a ten is a ten-pound note
E is short for English
rife means widespread, plentiful

explanation.surface: A tourist abroad notices English spoken everywhere.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition points to a place you might go on holiday; Tenerife is a Canary Island famous for British tourists.
explanation.definitionFit: Tenerife is a holiday island, somewhere you might be on vacation.

clue.text: Check over golf rule (5)

indicators.note: REIN goes over G, covering it on both sides

blocks.note: to rein in is to check
G is golf in the NATO alphabet

explanation.surface: Look over the rules of golf.
explanation.walkthrough: "Check over" reads as "review"; "Check" is the curb REIN and "over" wraps it round G.
explanation.definitionFit: A plain synonym, as noun or verb: a monarch's period on the throne, or holding power over a kingdom.

clue.text: Straight face worthless, I suspect (2,3,4,5)

indicators.note: the letters are dubious, not to be taken as they stand

blocks.note: anagram fodder, 14 letters

explanation.surface: A poker player suspects a deadpan expression hides a worthless hand.
explanation.walkthrough: "Straight face" reads as one phrase; split it so "Straight" is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: An idiom for distance measured directly, ignoring roads, since a bird takes the straight route.

clue.text: It’s coated in oils for nibbles (8)

indicators.note: IT is covered by the outer letters

blocks.note: crudes are crude oils
the clue's own word

explanation.surface: Party snacks are dressed in oil.
explanation.walkthrough: The ’s is "is": IT is coated in CRUDES. Crudités are raw vegetable sticks served with dips.
explanation.definitionFit: Crudités are raw vegetables served as nibbles.

clue.text: Liberal working with fellow author (6)

blocks.note: L for Liberal
a machine that is on is working
a don is a college fellow

explanation.surface: A Liberal politician co-writes a book with a colleague.
explanation.walkthrough: Jack London wrote The Call of the Wild. "Fellow" reads as a companion; it is a university fellow, a don.
explanation.definitionFit: Definition by example: Jack, the American who wrote White Fang, is one author among many.
